overview: The committee approved a student-led project to plant a fruit orchard at Medford High School and established a randomization process to address an enrollment imbalance between the city's middle schools. The meeting also included departmental budget reports and a new rule restricting the use of electronic devices by members during public sessions.

items.title: Administrative approvals
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from April and May, as well as warrants and payrolls, following a brief inquiry into out-of-district vocational tuition costs.

items.title: One Mission Buzz Off fundraiser
items.summary: Anthony Petrellis and Chris Murphy promoted a community fundraiser for pediatric cancer involving a head-shaving event at John Brewer’s Tavern.

items.title: Medford High School fruit orchard
items.summary: Approved a student proposal from the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility to plant a fruit orchard on the high school campus. The project will be supported by community donations and student volunteers.

items.title: Student recognition for foreign language
items.summary: Recognized sophomore Cheng Cheng for earning a gold medal and international study trip for her performance on the National Italian Exam.

items.title: Kindergarten enrollment and orientation
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Diane Caldwell reported on kindergarten orientation efforts and noted an increase of 13 students compared to the previous year.

items.title: Columbus Afterschool Math Tutoring Program
items.summary: Received a report on a pilot math program at Columbus Elementary, with discussion focused on reducing group sizes and using data for more targeted student selection next year.

items.title: Seal of Biliteracy and Foreign Language budget
items.summary: Approved the implementation of the State Seal of Biliteracy for graduating seniors and received the department’s pre-budget report. The committee also acknowledged the upcoming retirement of director Rita DeCarlo.

items.title: Student trip to Italy
items.summary: Approved a student educational trip to Italy scheduled for April 2019.

items.title: English Learner Department report
items.summary: Approved a departmental report outlining plans to redesign the middle school program and requesting additional staff to accommodate a 40-student increase in EL enrollment.

items.title: Lesley University partnership RFP
items.summary: Voted to issue a Request for Proposals for a university partnership to fund renovations to the high school gymnasium in exchange for facility use.

items.title: Middle school placement and randomization
items.summary: Approved a plan to use a randomization process to move approximately 15 to 20 students from the Brooks and Roberts schools to the McGlynn Middle School to balance enrollment. The committee directed the incoming McGlynn principal to meet with affected parents before the final selection.

items.title: Electronic device policy and routine items
items.summary: Accepted a quarterly collaborative report and adopted a new rule restricting members from using electronic devices for private deliberations during public meetings.

items.title: Recess legislation resolution
items.summary: Approved a resolution in support of state bills that would mandate 20 minutes of daily unstructured recess as time on learning.
